name: imp

attributes.attribute: a figure in British folklore, a term once applied to a tree cutting and later to fairy people seen as children of the Devil
fully a Christian concept, absent from the beliefs of the pre-Christian Celtic people

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: An imp is a figure in British folklore. The old word imp, also spelled ymp, meant a cutting from a tree. During Puritan times the term came to name fairy people. These were seen as offshoots of the Devil. The idea is fully a Christian one. The pre-Christian people of Celtic lands did not believe in a specific force of evil. They did not hold that the people of the Otherworld were the children of evil.

okr.objective: Document the British folkloric figure the imp.
key_results: Record the old meaning of imp, or ymp, as a tree cutting.
Record the Puritan-era shift of the term to fairy people.
Note that the concept is wholly Christian.
